questions.prompt: Inside `DisplayTotal()`, the local function `Show()` prints `total`, a local variable declared in `DisplayTotal()` with the value 100. What happens when `Show()` is called?
options: It does not compile, because local functions can't see the enclosing method's variables
It prints `Total = 0`, because `total` is copied before it is set
It prints `Total = 100`, because local functions can capture variables from the outer method

questions.prompt: Which statement about top-level statements is true?
options: Every file in the project can contain its own top-level statements
You cannot declare any other types in a program that uses top-level statements
Each statement is wrapped in its own generated class
Only one file in the project can contain top-level statements; the compiler wraps them in a generated `Main` method
questions.explanation: The compiler creates a hidden `Program` class and wraps your statements in a generated `Main` method, and only one file in the project can contain top-level statements. Other types can still be declared below the top-level code.

questions.prompt: `User` declares `public required string Name { get; set; }` and `public required string Email { get; set; }`. What happens with `var user = new User();`?
options: It compiles, and `Name` and `Email` are set to empty strings
It fails to compile, because the required members are not initialized
It compiles but throws a `NullReferenceException` at run time
It compiles, but the compiler shows a warning only
questions.explanation: With `required` (C# 11), the compiler forces initialization, so `new User()` without setting `Name` and `Email` is a compile error; `new User { Name = ..., Email = ... }` works.

questions.prompt: Why are default interface methods (C# 8) useful?
options: They let an interface hold instance fields
They force every implementing class to override the method
They let you add new methods to an existing interface without breaking existing implementations
They allow a class to inherit from multiple classes
questions.explanation: A default body means classes that don't override the method still work, which gives backward compatibility and avoids repeating shared logic.
